references.text: Parallel text in the same chapter describing the same action with the oil that the priest is to put on the one being cleansed, to make atonement for him.
Describes how the priest is to use the oil on the one being cleansed, including on the head, as part of the cleansing ritual.
Moses poured anointing oil on Aaron's head, a similar ritual with oil on the head for consecration and sanctification.
The anointing oil is poured on the head as part of priestly consecration, the same symbolic action with oil on the head.
The priest makes atonement for the person, and he receives forgiveness - using the same language about atonement (לְכַפֵּר) before the Lord.
The priest is to make atonement for him for his sin - uses the same expression לְכַפֵּר עָלָיו for atonement.

Describes how almost everything is cleansed with blood according to the law, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness - linking this Old Testament atonement ritual to Christ's perfect sacrifice.
